sector_model: nonfinancial industrial technology (connectors, sensors, cable); GAAP earnings, FCF after capex, net debt after a large acquisition
thesis: Amphenol (interconnect, sensors, antennas for AI data center, industrial, mobile and automotive markets) reported Q3 2026 sales 10,229.7M (+65% y/y) and net income 2,034.3M (+63%), with 9M sales +59.8% helped by the CommScope connectivity business bought on 2026-01-09 for part of 11.06B of 2026 acquisitions. Close 74.59 on 2026-11-06 (NYSE, post 2-for-1 split) gives market cap about 184.2B: 31.1x TTM GAAP earnings, FCF yield 2.8%, net debt about 12.6B. Quality is high, but price already assumes durable AI-related demand.
counterthesis: Growth is mostly acquired and TTM figures understate the deal's cost; organic growth was not read. At 31x earnings and a 2.8% FCF yield the shares price continued AI infrastructure strength. Net debt rose from about 4.1B to 12.6B and goodwill from 10.6B to 17.7B in nine months. The stock dropped 9.3% on 2026-11-05 (79.01 to 71.64) and cause is unconfirmed. Share-count gap between cover (2,469M) and diluted (2,583M) is unexplained. MD&A, FY2025 10-K and peers not read.
invalidation: Organic growth turning negative or falling below high single digits; net debt/EBITDA rising above 2.5x; CommScope integration margin dilution; AI data center order slowdown; goodwill impairment.
